suggestion: Use only a dated team-issued depth chart or licensed primary feed for starter/backup order; otherwise keep the rank blank.
benefit_for_decisions: Supports offense and defense replacement research without inferring a player’s string rank from roster order.
main_risk: A roster page is not a depth chart; access and reuse rights may be restricted.
options: A) Obtain written permission for an official team chart; B) license a provider with explicit model-use rights; C) defer rank and leave it blank.

suggestion: Collect official schedule, scores and box scores for past seasons
benefit_for_decisions: Creates the history needed for any validation gate
main_risk: Scale of collection
options: A) Request licensed historical NFL results and box-score access; B) use a provider with explicit archive/model rights; C) keep historical values blank and publish source links only.

suggestion: Choose an odds data provider and review its terms
benefit_for_decisions: Needed to compare our lines with the market and measure closing line value
main_risk: Provider access, historical completeness, permitted model use, market coverage and jurisdiction are unknown.
options: A) Request a written licensed quote and reuse terms; B) compare authorized providers; C) do not use odds and keep line/price fields blank.

suggestion: Archive injury-report versions only under written permission or an authorized feed, preserving publication and capture timestamps.
benefit_for_decisions: Allows tracking of status changes across the week
main_risk: Systematic retrieval is restricted by NFL.com terms absent express written consent; public-page availability does not grant archive rights.
options: A) Obtain permission and define retention; B) license an authorized historical feed; C) keep source links only and leave historical status changes blank.

suggestion: Add lightweight filters for review; do not add bulk CSV export for NFL data until written rights permit it.
benefit_for_decisions: Easier review of rows
main_risk: Export could reproduce or redistribute NFL data without a license; filters should not become a collection mechanism.
options: A) Filters only for currently licensed/authorized fields; B) export only project metadata; C) defer export until written rights are cleared.

suggestion: Keep source, license, validation and scope approvals traceable in the project record; consider a dedicated page only if needed.
benefit_for_decisions: Keeps data-use permissions, methodology and implementation decisions auditable.
main_risk: Duplicates COORDINATION.md
options: A) Continue using COORDINATION.md; B) add a decision page only if multiple reviewers need it.

suggestion: Consider an automated refresh only after the data provider grants written permission and the update/retention method is reviewed.
benefit_for_decisions: Keeps injury data current without manual work
main_risk: Requires an authorized feed and workflow permissions; do not automate scraping of NFL.com pages.
options: A) Scheduled workflow using a licensed feed; B) manual source links without copying/archive; C) no refresh until rights are cleared.

suggestion: Pre-register validation design and decision criteria before tests; leave unsupported numeric cutoffs blank until a qualified statistical review.
benefit_for_decisions: Reduces post-hoc selection while avoiding invented NFL-specific sample-size or significance thresholds.
main_risk: Criteria cannot be selected responsibly before market, data rights, and eligible sample are defined.
options: A) Pre-register with a statistician after data access is approved; B) publish methodology without a performance ranking; C) defer the leaderboard.

suggestion: Run timestamped no-stakes forecasts prospectively before ranking strategies; choose the duration and acceptance rule only in a pre-registered plan.
benefit_for_decisions: Creates an auditable test of skill versus variance; prospective tracking reduces hindsight but cannot eliminate randomness or guarantee outcomes.
main_risk: No universal number of weeks or bets establishes skill; outcome and price data must be rights-cleared.
options: A) Define a prospective period after data/legal gates; B) require untouched out-of-time evaluation; C) publish no leaderboard until those tests exist.

suggestion: Obtain qualified legal review of the exact product, audience, wager/referral/reward mechanics, and each target jurisdiction before any real-money or prize feature.
benefit_for_decisions: Avoids treating Japan-specific online-betting guidance as a ruling on every contest or other jurisdiction.
main_risk: Legal treatment depends on product mechanics, user location and applicable jurisdiction; this official guidance is Japan-specific.
options: A) Obtain jurisdiction-specific advice first (recommended); B) keep this site no-stakes and reward-free; C) do not launch the affected feature.

suggestion: Extend the results dataset to earlier seasons from the official by-week schedule pages, re-fit and re-gate every strategy.
benefit_for_decisions: 89 out-of-sample games is below the roughly 200+ games needed to resolve a one-point edge; more seasons shrink the confidence intervals.
main_risk: NFL.com terms restrict systematic retrieval — secure written permission first (F16).
options: A) Request written permission for bulk historical results; B) license a provider with model-use rights; C) stay single-season and publish wide intervals.

suggestion: Add two or three official team-stat inputs (yards per play, turnovers, third-down rate) to the totals model, with cross-validated shrinkage.
benefit_for_decisions: Totals currently show no measurable skill (-0.11 points vs a constant baseline); this is the cheapest way to find out whether they can.
main_risk: More parameters on 89 games raises overfit risk; every added input needs its own out-of-sample test.
options: A) Add inputs one at a time and keep the best by out-of-sample error; B) leave totals unmodelled and say so.

suggestion: Keep the naive reference line published next to every originated line, and never describe a win against it as a win against a sportsbook.
benefit_for_decisions: Prevents the single most likely misreading of the leaderboard: a 72% hit rate against a noisy benchmark is not a 72% win rate against a market price.
main_risk: None — it is a labelling discipline.
options: A) Publish both numbers side by side (as now); B) hide the bet columns and show forecast accuracy only.

suggestion: Pre-register next season's strategies, markets, bet thresholds and gates in a frozen spec file before Week 1, then grade them prospectively.
benefit_for_decisions: Removes selection bias: today's leaderboard was graded on the same 89 games that were used to choose the model family, which inflates apparent skill.
main_risk: Requires a frozen specification and the discipline not to change it mid-season.
options: A) Freeze a spec file before Week 1 and grade only against it; B) keep grading retrospectively but pay the multiple-comparison penalty and label results exploratory.

suggestion: Do not launch player-prop or parlay products until leg outcomes, prices and settlement rules exist in the repository.
benefit_for_decisions: 24 tickets and one correlation estimate cannot price a parlay; no player-prop outcome exists here at all.
main_risk: Slower roadmap.
options: A) Wait for rights-cleared data; B) run a private, clearly-labelled paper tracker with the sample size shown on every row.

suggestion: Capture the same units every week (QB, OL, DL, DB) so exposure can be differenced over time instead of read from one snapshot.
benefit_for_decisions: Turns a single Week 10 snapshot into a time series that can actually be correlated with results; the current one-week correlation (r=-0.064) means nothing.
main_risk: Requires weekly capture plus written permission for storage and reuse (F16).
options: A) Capture weekly under written permission; B) keep ad-hoc snapshots and report no injury signal.

suggestion: Confirm the operating jurisdiction and obtain qualified legal review before any reward, entry fee, referral or wager mechanic is enabled.
benefit_for_decisions: Earlier sessions documented Japan-specific guidance while this session's account location is in the Netherlands (Kansspelautoriteit is the regulator there); neither jurisdiction is confirmed by the owner.
main_risk: Cost and delay.
options: A) Confirm the jurisdiction, then obtain qualified review; B) keep the project research-only with no rewards and no wagering.

suggestion: Show the required sample size and the shortfall next to every leaderboard row.
benefit_for_decisions: Makes 'not yet proven' visible: a strategy can rank first on skill and still be hundreds of games short of a decisive test.
main_risk: None.
options: A) Show both numbers, as built; B) hide them and show a single pass/fail column.

suggestion: Decide now whether to buy an authorised odds feed, because nothing else can turn accuracy into a profitability claim.
benefit_for_decisions: Without prices there is no closing-line value, no expected value per stake and no way to grade a strategy as profitable rather than merely accurate. Every profitability column on the site stays empty until this is decided.
main_risk: Provider access, historical completeness, permitted model use and jurisdiction are unknown.
options: A) Request a written licensed quote and reuse terms; B) compare authorised providers; C) stay results-only and keep every price column blank.

suggestion: Decide whether to pursue a licensed historical injury archive before building any availability-driven rule.
benefit_for_decisions: Historical injury reports are not retrievable from the public page, so any injury term added to the model today would be unvalidated. Buying the archive is the only path that makes those rules testable.
main_risk: Cost, licence scope, and whether model use is permitted at all.
options: A) License a dated injury archive with model-use rights; B) request written league permission; C) accept that availability rules stay unvalidated and out of the line.

suggestion: Adopt the walk-forward harness as the standing gate, and pre-register every new rule before it is scored.
benefit_for_decisions: Scoring a rule after seeing the results it explains is how false skill gets published. Pre-registration plus the existing eight gates makes each new claim falsifiable.
main_risk: Slows down exploration; that is the point.
options: A) Require a written rule definition and gate plan before scoring; B) allow exploratory scoring but label it exploratory and never rank it; C) no process.

suggestion: Keep the multiple-comparison adjustment, and treat a rule that fails it as unqualified even when its interval looks good.
benefit_for_decisions: Three rules currently look better than chance but none survives the adjustment for having tested eight. Publishing the adjustment is what keeps the leaderboard honest.
main_risk: It will keep the leaderboard empty for a while.
options: A) Keep the adjustment as the standing rule; B) move to a pre-registered single primary rule and drop the adjustment for it; C) drop the adjustment (not recommended).

suggestion: Do not act on the model total until it beats simply projecting the league average.
benefit_for_decisions: Right now it does not: 11.25 points of error against 11.04 for the naive baseline. Shipping a number that loses to a constant would waste attention and invite false confidence.
main_risk: Totals remain unavailable as a signal until the sample grows.
options: A) Keep the total published but labelled as the weakest number; B) suppress the total column until it beats the baseline; C) keep publishing it unlabelled (not recommended).

suggestion: Keep player props and parlays blocked until licensed player-level data and prices exist.
benefit_for_decisions: No player outcome, prop price or parlay settlement definition is available from an official source. Publishing a prop or parlay expectation would be invention, not research.
main_risk: Delays a part of the brief that the user asked for.
options: A) License player data and prices with model-use rights; B) build the framework only and publish it as untested; C) publish estimates anyway (not recommended).

suggestion: Record a UTC capture timestamp for every read and show it on every page.
benefit_for_decisions: The standings and the injury report were captured at different moments, and neither page states its own update time. A recorded timestamp removes the ambiguity.
main_risk: None.
options: A) Add a timestamp column to every data file; B) show a per-page as-of line; C) leave as is.

suggestion: Re-run the line-by-line injury and standings reconciliation on every future refresh, and fail the build if it does not pass.
benefit_for_decisions: The reconciliation is what caught nothing this time and proved the data clean. Making it a build step means a future transcription error cannot ship silently.
main_risk: A refresh with a genuine source change would block the build until reviewed.
options: A) Wire both checks into scripts/build.py as hard failures (standings check already added); B) run them manually; C) drop them.
status: For review — partially implemented (standings check wired)

suggestion: Define the leaderboard reward as non-monetary recognition, or leave it disabled, until legal review is complete.
benefit_for_decisions: The brief asks for rewards. Official Japan-specific guidance says online sports betting accessed from Japan is prohibited, and no qualified review has been done for a skill contest or reward design elsewhere.
main_risk: Designing a reward before legal review could create exposure.
options: A) Leave the reward disabled and rank rules for research only; B) define non-monetary recognition after review; C) proceed to a monetary reward without review (not recommended).

suggestion: Choose one of three paths on NFL data rights before the next expansion: written league permission, a licensed provider, or links-only.
benefit_for_decisions: NFL.com terms prohibit systematic retrieval to compile a database absent express prior written consent, and no permission is recorded for the published snapshot. Every further step depends on resolving this.
main_risk: Each path has cost or scope consequences.
options: A) Request written permission for the existing and future use; B) migrate to a licensed provider and re-source the data; C) reduce the site to commentary and links, keeping no copied data.

suggestion: Connect one licensed, rights-cleared odds feed to fill the price-snapshot store.
benefit_for_decisions: The price-snapshot store records opening and closing numbers for every originated market but every value is blank because no official free source publishes them. A licensed feed is the only way to fill the store and compute closing-line value and ROI.
main_risk: Without prices, no market comparison, CLV or ROI can ever be computed (F07/F31/F43).
options: A) License an odds feed and fill the store; B) request written league permission for a specific dataset; C) leave the store blank and flagged (current state).

suggestion: Approve the demotion gate rule and the gate cut-offs before any strategy is promoted to live.
benefit_for_decisions: The demotion gate (G9) is defined but the numeric cut-offs (F17) and the qualification disagreement (F42) are unresolved, so no strategy is live. Approving the rule makes the gate operable.
main_risk: Promoting a strategy before the gates are approved would bypass the safeguard.
options: A) Approve the gates and the demotion rule, then promote on a fresh pre-registered test; B) keep everything Paper until then (current state); C) promote without approval (not recommended).

suggestion: Pre-register one primary strategy and a fixed sample to settle the qualification disagreement.
benefit_for_decisions: Two independent implementations disagree on how many strategies qualify (F42). A pre-registered primary rule and sample would resolve it without manufacturing significance.
main_risk: The disagreement blocks any live promotion and any reward (F42).
options: A) Pre-register one primary rule and a fixed sample, then test once; B) combine both implementations into a single pre-registered test; C) ignore the disagreement (not recommended).

suggestion: Adopt a fixed snapshot cadence for the fair line: origin at origination, one interim snapshot per week, close at the scheduled kickoff.
benefit_for_decisions: The store records one fair value per market (the origin). With a fixed cadence the fair open/close series gains real content, line movement becomes measurable on our own numbers, and the store is ready to compare against a market feed the day one is authorised.
main_risk: Interim snapshots add rows; they are our own model outputs, so no new rights exposure.
options: A) Adopt the cadence and record it in model_summary.json; B) record origin and close only; C) leave the cadence unset.

suggestion: Add a formula unit-test harness for every published statistic after the C09 formula error (F48).
benefit_for_decisions: C09 carried a correlation interval applied to a regression slope across several review passes. A small test file (known-value cases per formula: Fisher CI, slope CI, Wilson interval, permutation p, BH q) would catch the next defect before publication.
main_risk: None - tests only; no published value changes unless a test finds a defect.
options: A) Add scripts/test_formulas.py with known-value cases and wire it into the build order; B) review by hand each pass; C) do nothing.

suggestion: Add a computed masking-check verdict to the signal/staking register: flag a positive staking record whose signal interval includes zero, and the reverse.
benefit_for_decisions: The brief requires staking luck not to mask a bad signal. Ranking already uses signal only; an explicit computed column makes any masking visible at a glance instead of requiring the reader to compare two intervals by hand.
main_risk: None - derived from published intervals; no new claim.
options: A) Add the column in the signal/staking generator; B) keep the prose rule only; C) drop the check.

suggestion: Run the line-book capture on a fixed cadence and let the store's contract check report any market that reaches kickoff with no closing capture.
benefit_for_decisions: Turns 'we record opening and closing numbers' from a schema into something that either happens or is visibly reported as not having happened; a missing closing number cannot be recovered after kickoff, so the only useful control is the deadline.
effort: Low - the capture and the check exist (scripts/line_book.py capture / --check); what is missing is a schedule.
main_risk: Cadence drifts if nobody runs it; a snapshot store with stale rows looks authoritative.
options: A) run it at T-24h and T-2h before each kickoff; B) run it on every build; C) leave it manual and accept that most closings will be missing.

suggestion: Wire scripts/results_feed.py grade into the build so an originated market with no settlement path fails the build rather than being quietly absent.
benefit_for_decisions: The brief asks for a results feed 'so backtests and ROI can be computed at all'. A feed that omits a fixture silently is worse than no feed, because the gap becomes invisible; making the join a build requirement means a new line cannot be published unless the grader can see the fixture.
effort: Low - the grade join already reports orphans (0 today), so this is a one-line build hook.
main_risk: A build that fails on a missing result can also fail on a league-wide postponement; the rule needs an explicit 'scheduled and unsettled is fine, absent is not' state, which the feed already carries.
options: A) fail the build on an absent fixture; B) warn only; C) leave it manual.

suggestion: Publish a three-way home / tie / away probability, or state explicitly that ties are treated as pushes, and put the tie count on the page that shows the moneyline.
benefit_for_decisions: Removes a whole category of later argument about what a published probability meant, at a cost of one number per game. The season already contains a tie, so this is not hypothetical polish.
effort: Low-medium - the derived probability is a one-line change in the origination step; the leaderboard and grade table need a tie outcome.
main_risk: Changing the definition mid-season breaks comparability with graded history; if adopted, adopt it from the next full week and say so.
options: A) three-way; B) keep two-way, ties push, stated on the page; C) keep as is with the bias documented (F58).

suggestion: Publish per-strategy error columns in the backtest file and let every gate read from published columns only.
benefit_for_decisions: Today a reviewer who wants to check a gate for M2, M3, M4 or T1 has to re-implement the scorer (this session did, and had to first prove its scorer matched the published M1 column). Publishing the columns makes the gates checkable by anyone without the model.
effort: Low - the predictions are already in the file; the errors are one subtraction each.
main_risk: More columns to keep in sync with the model; a mismatch between a published error and a recomputed one becomes a visible defect (that is arguably the point).
options: A) add the columns; B) publish the scorer as a small library instead; C) leave it.

suggestion: Treat a club-chart omission as 'this source cannot place the player', never as 'the player is fine', and store the fetch time on every depth row.
benefit_for_decisions: Three Week 10 report players appear on no row of their own club chart (F63). A pipeline that reads a chart omission as an absence of injury would invent data in exactly the place the brief says to leave a blank.
effort: Low - the register already carries chart_read_on and a blank_reason field.
main_risk: A chart is an alignment snapshot, so its information decays; an undated fetch is a wrong fetch.
options: A) keep fetch time mandatory and blank on omission (current); B) allow third-party charts with a label; C) drop depth from the pipeline until charts are licensed.

suggestion: Require BOTH the rolling window and the full window to fail before a demotion fires, and record the window length in the pre-registration rather than in the gate text.
benefit_for_decisions: At n=50 the drafted D1 demotes everything measured today (F54, and this session's demotion_evaluation.csv agrees). A gate that always fires is not a control, it is noise; a gate that never fires is worse. Requiring both windows keeps the early-warning property without making the rolling window decisive on its own.
effort: Low - it changes the rule text and one comparison in the evaluation script.
main_risk: Two-condition gates demote later; a genuinely broken strategy runs longer before the gate acts.
options: A) both windows must fail; B) rolling only (current draft); C) rolling for review, full for demotion.

suggestion: Number board claims from a single counter file, and re-read the board immediately before writing a claim.
benefit_for_decisions: This session and session 8a0bf37e both claimed overlapping task IDs on the same day (T42-T49 twice) and both picked F56+ ranges, because the board's highest number is buried 600 lines deep in a 91 KB file. The registers survived because both sessions re-numbered on finding the collision, but the same race could have silently overwritten rows.
effort: Low - a one-line counter file (next_task, next_flag, next_src, next_q, next_s, next_r) that each session increments in its claim commit.
main_risk: Two sessions increment the counter in the same minute and collide anyway; a commit hook or a single-writer convention is needed for that.
options: A) counter file; B) session-ID prefixed identifiers (T-e4e71368-01); C) keep as is.
